perspective:
Angela’s accessible perspective includes:

- She is Angela Hwang, a hairdresser with a doctorate. She and Kevin Flores have been close friends since high school; despite different career paths, they confide in each other. She knows Kevin is a construction worker and has noticed he seems unhappy at work.
- Coffee meeting: She invited Kevin to coffee. She heard Kevin say he was “alright,” just the usual grind; he admitted he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was going through the motions. She told him she was worried and asked if he had considered a different job or career path. He said he had thought about it but did not know where to start and felt overwhelmed. She suggested figuring it out together and looking into options; he agreed and thanked her for her support.
- Resources: She found job openings and a career counseling service and told Kevin about them. He thanked her and said he had been thinking a lot and was interested in something more creative, maybe design or architecture. She encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would. She believed he was considering a career change and felt supportive and hopeful.
- Career coach: She believed Kevin was hesitant. She felt frustrated and worried. She arranged a meeting with a career coach and told Kevin. He said she did not have to do that, appreciated it, but was not sure he was ready. She encouraged him that a push and the coach could help him make a plan and gain confidence. He agreed to give it a shot. She promised to support him.
- Progress: She believed Kevin was making progress and felt proud and relieved. She asked how things were going with the career coach. Kevin told her the coach had been helpful, he had started online courses in design, and he felt more confident. She offered more help; he said knowing she was there was enough and he would ask if he needed anything.
- Celebration: She believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career and felt happy and satisfied. She organized a small celebration party and told him. He thanked her. She said he deserved it, had worked hard, and had come far. He said he was grateful and could not have done it without her. She said he did the hard work and suggested enjoying the party; he agreed.
